goal: Same three-view sheet and seeds as female-raccoon-001-baseline-ipadapter, but with: teal #48C2C3 fur (not pale seafoam); a mint chest (not cream) and a mint hip patch, as in baseline-highres.png; navy that reads as blue #2A4365 (001's came out near-black/purple in all four); white inner ears; and no hourglasses, arrows, hooks, tiaras, devil tails, limb studies or logo tiles in the empty space.
why: BASE: female-raccoon-001-baseline-ipadapter (Josh: off-track). Same model, charsheet_lora_v1:0.6, 1536x1024, 30 steps, CFG 6, Euler a, seeds 20261027-20261030, so images compare one to one. TWO CHANGES, judged on different parts of the image (figure colours vs. empty background). CHANGE 1, COLOUR: IP-Adapter weight 0.5 -> 0.8 (same ip-adapter-plus_sdxl_vit-h, CLIP-ViT-H, same reference). At 0.5, 001 got pale seafoam fur, cream chest, near-black/purple navy and no hip patch. At 0.8 the reference's saturated teal, blue navy and mint (and the hip patch in its back view) weigh much more in the conditioning. The weight is not the only colour lever: replacing 'clean lineart' (change 2c) may also improve colour, since 'lineart' pulls toward uncoloured, washed-out images on this model. So better colour can't be credited to 0.8 alone. The colour words are left as they were; if fur stays seafoam or the chest cream, suspect the 'pale mint'/'off-white' wording next. LAYOUT: 'Balanced' control mode likely has little effect on an IP-Adapter in Forge (it works through attention, not ControlNet residuals). Only the prompt guards against copying the reference's four-figure layout: '(three views:1.2)', 'same character three times', and the negatives '(color swatch:1.2)', '(color palette:1.3)', 'bust', 'head studies'. CHANGE 2, STRAY OBJECTS (wording only): (a) '(hourglass figure:1.2)' removed from the positive; it drew literal hourglasses in 3 of 4. The build stays on '(narrow waist:1.1), (wide hips:1.1)', unchanged from 001. (b) '(no clothes, no accessories:1.2)' removed (CLIP reads 'no X' as X, likely the tiara). 'accessories, jewelry, tiara' added to the negative beside 'clothes'; '(featureless body:1.3)' keeps the plain body (001 review rec 3). (c) 'clean lineart' -> 'clean bold outlines' (style guide wording; 'thick outlines' stays). 'lineart' tags uncoloured line drawings, matching 001's outline figures and studies. '(sketches:1.2)' is added to the negative by this job to back this up. (d) New negatives for what the LoRA drew in the empty space: '(props:1.3), objects, (hourglass:1.3), (arrows:1.2), symbols, icons, logo, (sketches:1.2), (extra tails:1.2), (devil tail:1.2)'. No anatomy words in the negative (enoch-rules.md censor-mark rule). WHY BUNDLED: props wording alone at 0.5 would just repeat the colour failure; weight alone would repeat the hourglasses on these seeds. Overlap: a stronger IP-Adapter may also tidy the background (the reference has no clutter), so a clean background can't be credited fully to the wording. RISKS: at 0.8 the reference's swatches (incl. the yellow dot), side bust or fourth figure may leak; read that as the weight too high. NOT TESTED: head size (needs a female edge guide from Josh), stronger '(teal fur)' wording, and 001 review recs 1-2 (layout).
